episode_title: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

real_qa.q: What are the main stages of FDA drug development pipeline that procurement teams need to understand?
real_qa.r: The FDA has a very structured pipeline with core drug discovery in the laboratory, preclinical testing involving animal testing for safety and toxicity, and then clinical trials with three main phases. Each phase involves setting up endpoints and design of experiments, with discussions between the medical community, researchers, and the FDA about what those endpoints mean before conducting the actual trials.

real_qa.q: What role do Contract Research Organizations (CROs) play in pharmaceutical drug development?
real_qa.r: CROs are professional service firms with staff including PhDs and highly skilled people who understand how to run tests in both preclinical areas focusing on animal testing and in human trials. They help structure the design of experiments, manage clinical trial management systems for data capture, handle regulatory oversight, and provide documentation for FDA presentation.
real_qa.requete: what are CROs contract research organizations pharma

real_qa.q: How should procurement manage costs when biotech companies scale from early-stage to clinical trials?
real_qa.r: Companies may scale spending from $20 million annually to $40 million, then $80 million, $100 million, and potentially $200 million per year in drug development. Procurement needs more structured finance, legal, and formal agreements as budgets grow, with provisions for controlled costs, pass-through costs, and areas for adjustment when unknowns occur during trials.
real_qa.requete: biotech drug development budget scaling costs

real_qa.q: What is the Viagra pivot case and what does it teach about drug discovery flexibility?
real_qa.r: Viagra was initially designed for heart treatment more than 20 years ago, but during trials it showed different indications that led to a different marketplace and different aspect of human health. This demonstrates the importance of maintaining collaborative supplier relationships and curiosity rather than rigid agreements, so companies can uncover unexpected pivots and create an innovative culture.
real_qa.requete: Viagra drug discovery pivot heart treatment

real_qa.q: How should procurement teams build relationships with internal R&D teams in pharma companies?
real_qa.r: Procurement must actively seek out R&D staff through coffee meetings and lunches to listen and understand their needs rather than waiting for them to approach. Instead of acting as a budget master or imposing bureaucratic constraints, procurement should find common vocabulary around regulatory and scientific aspects, help them maximize value from budgets, and continuously cultivate trusted relationships while flexing on parameters as projects evolve.

real_qa.q: What happens to pharma companies when procurement fails to manage drug development supplier costs?
real_qa.r: If costs get out of hand, the company will lose money and might experience failures. In very risky early-stage investments, this can mean bankruptcy. This is why supporting supplier relationships and putting parameters around contracts to manage costs is critical to the success of the drug development process.
real_qa.requete: pharma bankruptcy drug development cost control
